v1.feedback: The chalice silhouette is well-constructed with anatomically distinct regions and the damped-spring boing mechanic is a genuinely charming surprise that maps the word prompt directly to differential physics per region — tendrils whip, base squashes, knop pivots. Consider tightening the crown tendrils: with reach up to 5 units and spreading scatter, the top 24% of particles may dissolve into sparse noise above the rim, weakening the silhouette read; capping tendril reach at ~2.5 and increasing particle density there would keep the chalice outline crisp. The 0.9 z-scale flattening on every region is a subtle cheat for front-view framing but reads as slightly pancaked under orbit drag — either commit to a bas-relief presentation with locked orbit, or let z breathe at full scale.

v2.feedback: The five-region chalice anatomy is well-structured and the per-region boing propagation (base anchored, tendrils whip) is the strongest idea here — it gives the 'boing' word real physical character rather than just a uniform bounce. Two refinements: the crown tendrils with reach up to 2.5 units risk softening the chalice silhouette into a fuzzy halo — tighten reach to ~1.5 or increase tendril particle density so they read as solid organic extensions rather than scatter. Second, the gather animation (particles coalesce from scatter) and the periodic boing compete for attention as the two motion events — consider starting already gathered so the boing is the sole surprise, or make the gather happen only once on load and never repeat.
